_comment: Pronunciation lexicon for Video G (narration skill, PRONUNCIATION.md). Only respell and accept change narration; say/ipa/lang/sources/decoy/note/probe are the record. Names and terms the script speaks: Lie, Sophus, Euler, Rodrigues, Chasles, Mozzi, Brockett, KUKA, Apollo, Collins, Jacobian, Newton, gimbal. On screen only, not here: quaternion, iiwa (no source of record for its pronunciation). Lie and Euler copied from Video J's record; the rest looked up with lookup_pronunciation.py and corrected by hand where it guessed (Sophus, KUKA, Mozzi), each note says how. Probed with probe_names.py run --voice michael on 2026-10-13; each entry's probe.verdict says what the ASR heard and why that respelling was kept (plain spellings where michael reads the word right). The owner's pronunciation overrides every entry.

Lie.note: Sophus Lie, Norwegian [liː]: 'Lee'. Spoken at 15_4 ('Lie algebra', 'Lie group'). The ordinary spelling is not offered to the voice: it is the English word 'lie'. Copied from Video J's lexicon (same voice and ftts build); in this video spoken at 05_7 ('Sophus Lie'), 15_4 and 15_5 ('Lie group').

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: VERIFIED as in Video J: 'Lee' heard as Lee 3/3; the plain spelling and the decoy 'Lye' heard as lie/Lye/Lai. The tool says UNVERIFIED only because the decoy's 'lie' is the name's own spelling.

Euler.note: English usage; Wikipedia's lead notes that 'YOO-ler' is considered incorrect. Copied from Video J's lexicon (same voice and ftts build); in this video spoken at 02_4. The plain spelling fails in michael (heard YOO-ler, control 0/3), so the respelling matters.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PASS: Oiler and OY-ler heard as Euler 3/3; the plain spelling heard as EULA/Eula (YOO-ler) 2/3; the decoy YOO-ler heard differently.

Sophus.note: Marius Sophus Lie, Norwegian [ˈsûːfʉs] (Wikipedia's lead). English speakers often say SOH-fus; the owner's ear decides. The lookup tool returned 'Lee' here, the IPA of the surname, corrected by hand. Spoken at 05_7 ('Sophus Lie').

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PASS: Soofus heard as Sufus/Sufis 3/3, the SOO-fus target; the plain spelling read as Sofit/Sofa/Sophos; SOO-fus was read as letters. The owner may prefer the English SOH-fus.

Rodrigues.note: Olinde Rodrigues was French (Bordeaux), of a Portuguese-Jewish family; French [ʁɔdʁiɡ] is roh-DREEG. English usage for 'Rodrigues' formula' keeps the final s, close to the Spanish /roˈdɾiɡes/ in Wiktionary; no written source gives the English usage. Partial, for the owner's ear. Spoken at 05_6.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PARTIAL, for the owner's ear: the plain spelling heard as Rodrigues 2/3 (Roderick once); the respelling rod-REE-gez was read with a soft g (Rod Regis, Rejez), so it is dropped; the decoy ROD-ri-gooz was also heard once as Rodrigues, so the ASR does not settle the vowel. Check the 05_6 narration sheet.

Chasles.note: Michel Chasles, French [ʃal] (Wikipedia's lead): the s is silent. Spoken at 07_6.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PARTIAL 2/3: Shahl heard as Shal, Schaal (and Charles once); the plain spelling is read wrongly with the s sounded (Chassels, Chaz all); Shall was read as 'shall'. Check the 07_6 sheet.

sources: Italian orthography: intervocalic -zz- [tts] (Giulio Mozzi, Discorso matematico sopra il rotamento momentaneo dei corpi, 1763)
Mozzi.note: Giulio Mozzi, Italian; no article with a pronunciation was found. Italian orthography: zz between vowels is a long ts. Guessed from spelling, low confidence: for the owner's ear. Spoken at 07_6.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PARTIAL, low-confidence target (from Italian spelling): Motsee heard as MOTSI, Motzi, Motsi 3/3 (the tool counts 2/3); MOHT-see as Moatsy, Moatsi and once Mutt-C; the plain spelling is read MOZZ-ee (Mozzie, Muzzy), the decoy's sound. For the owner's ear.

Brockett.note: Roger Brockett, American; an English surname with regular spelling, stress first. No source gives its pronunciation. Spoken at 08_6.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: Plain spelling: heard as Brockett 2/3 (Rocket once, in the middle carrier); an ordinary English surname read as written. The ASR does not tell BROCK-it from bro-KET, so the stress is for the owner's ear.

KUKA.note: The German robot maker; the name began as an acronym (Keller und Knappich Augsburg) and is said as a word, KOO-kah, in German and in English trade use. The lookup tool assumed letters; the letters reading is the decoy. Spoken at 01_5 and 06_1.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PARTIAL: 'Kuka' heard as Kuka 2/3 (Hookah once), the word reading KOO-kah; the capitals KUKA were read unsteadily (Kukka, Kyugah) and the letters decoy was heard as KUKA, so the capitals are not offered to the voice. Check the 01_5 and 06_1 sheets.

Apollo.note: Apollo 11's guidance computer and gimbal lock. Spoken at 03_4 and 03_5.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PASS: the plain word heard as Apollo 3/3; the decoy APP-uh-loh heard differently.

Collins.note: Michael Collins, Apollo 11's command module pilot. Spoken at 03_5.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: Plain word: heard as Collins 2/3 (Colin once); KOL-inz was worse (Cullen, Cole Innes). An ordinary English name.

Jacobian.note: A term of art (some say yuh-KOH-bee-un, after Jacobi). Spoken at 10_3 and 13_4.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: Plain word: heard as Jacobian 2/3 (once garbled mid-sentence); the respelling juh-KOH-bee-un was read as letters (Jocko H.B.). Check the 10_3 and 13_4 sheets.

Newton.note: Newton's method at 13_6; US speech drops the y (NOO-tun), British keeps it (NYOO-tun).

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: Plain word: heard as Newton 3/3. The tool says UNVERIFIED because the plain spelling heard as itself proves nothing about the vowel; NOO-tun and NYOO-tun are both standard.

gimbal.note: Both JIM-bul (Wiktionary) and GIM-bul (Merriam-Webster's first) are standard; the ASR spells both 'gimbal', so the reading heard is for the owner's ear. Spoken at 03_1, 03_3, 03_5, 11_6.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: Plain word: heard as gimbal 3/3 (hard g, GIM-bul, Merriam-Webster's first reading). The tool's winner JIM-bul was heard as Jimbo, Jimble, Jim Bull, which would fail the line gate at 03_1, 03_3, 03_5 and 11_6, so it is not used; the owner may prefer JIM-bul.

Michel.note: Michel Chasles (07_6.0). The first narration read the plain spelling as the English Michael (heard 'Michael Schaal'); added after that pass, not yet probed: the next narration's line gate is its check.

Giulio.note: Giulio Mozzi (07_6.1). Read right as written: heard 'Giulio' in its take and 'Julio' (the same sound) in the line.
